grade.rationale: The stylesheet is coherent and uses shared design tokens consistently, but its fixed two-column layout can make the form unusable on narrow viewports, and the minified source formatting significantly reduces maintainability.

summary: One responsive-layout correctness issue and one source-readability issue were identified. Error presentation is styled appropriately, but test coverage is unknown; the supplied ESLint analysis was unavailable because its dependency was missing.

grade.rationale: The modal structure and scrolling constraints are generally sound, but the fixed-width sidebar can consume the entire dialog width on small screens.
Design-token usage is strong, but compressing numerous declarations and selectors onto each line makes changes and reviews unnecessarily difficult.
Selectors and class names are descriptive, although the minified formatting obscures rule boundaries and relationships.
Invalid fields and form-level errors receive clear, consistent visual treatment through dedicated selectors and severity tokens.
Stable semantic class selectors support UI testing, but the missing responsive behavior adds viewport-dependent risk. No coverage data was supplied.

findings.title: Fixed sidebar can collapse the form on narrow viewports
findings.description: The dialog width adapts to the viewport, but its first grid column always retains `--studio-modal-sidebar-width`. Once the available dialog width approaches or falls below that value, the `minmax(0,1fr)` form column can shrink to zero or become too narrow to use. The fieldset and footer controls have no compensating wrap or alternate mobile layout.
findings.recommendation: Add a narrow-viewport breakpoint that switches the body to a single-column layout or otherwise reduces/collapses the sidebar. Also allow option and action groups to wrap where necessary, and verify the dialog at representative mobile widths and enlarged text settings.

findings.title: Source stylesheet is stored in minified form
findings.description: Multiple selectors and all of their declarations are compressed onto long lines. This makes diffs harder to review, complicates precise diagnostics, and increases the chance of accidental edits affecting adjacent rules.
findings.recommendation: Format the source stylesheet with one declaration per line and conventional indentation. If minification is required for delivery, apply it only to generated build output through the existing build pipeline.
